headline: Japanese and South Korean shipyards are putting robots on welding and assembly lines to keep up with China.
score_reason: Industry trend with named targets, but read through a weak relay of the paywalled original.
importance_line: Shipyard workers in Korea and Japan may increasingly supervise machines rather than weld, as HD Hyundai and Hanwha Ocean chase China's 63% share of orders, though the figures are company targets reported by the FT and not independently checked.
summary: The Financial Times reports, as relayed by Hokanews, that shipbuilders in Japan and South Korea are speeding up the use of robots in their yards to offset labour shortages, ageing workforces and rising costs while Chinese yards hold 63% of global ship orders. HD Hyundai already uses robots for routine welding and targets partly unmanned factories by 2030, Hanwha Ocean says one worker can oversee up to 10 robots and aims to automate 70% of production, and robot maker Fanuc wants yards to run as many robots as people.
notes: Original FT blocked; text read on Hokanews (low-tier relay crediting FT via Coin Bureau). machine_action true: robots welding in HD Hyundai yards.
